subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
passage: Karthik spotted his grey stuffed elephant on the lowest shelf of the bookcase in their tenth-floor Pune flat, just above his head. He padded over, rose onto his toes and pushed his right arm up, grunting. His fingertips brushed the wood and slid off. He dropped back, swapped, and reached up with his left hand instead, face scrunched tight. His big sister Ankita looked up from her homework. "Almost, Karthik!"

qa.q: Which hand did Karthik try after his right arm fell short?
qa.a: He reached up with his left hand instead.

qa.q: What does Karthik's scrunched face suggest about how he feels?
qa.a: He seems determined and a bit frustrated: the first reach failed, but he grunts and keeps going with the other hand.

qa.q: What else could Karthik try when stretching is not enough?
qa.a: He could point at the elephant and look to Ankita for help, because asking reaches further than his arm can.

qa.q: How does Ankita see her little brother's effort?
qa.a: She finds it endearing and wants to encourage him, so she cheers because he is so close.

grounding: A toddler rises on tiptoe to reach a toy on a shelf and switches to the other hand when the first reach falls short.

subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
passage:
"Payal, what are you doing up there, jaan?" her mother Dilnaz called from the kitchen door.
"Ellie!" Payal jabbed a finger at the shelf, then went up on her toes. "Nnngh!"
"Your elephant? It's high today, na?"
Payal's left hand slapped the shelf edge, a finger short. "Uh!" She swapped, flinging her right hand higher.
"Other hand now? Still not there?"
"Ellie!" Payal wailed, straining again.
Dilnaz knelt beside her. "Shall we try together?"

qa.q: What name does Payal use for her elephant?
qa.a: She calls it "Ellie!"

qa.q: What was Payal feeling when she wailed "Ellie!" and strained again?
qa.a: She was frustrated and eager at once: she wanted the elephant badly, and both hands had come up short.

qa.q: Which approach would suit Payal better now, and why?
qa.a: Letting Dilnaz help, or asking with a point and a look, would work better, because her arms simply are not long enough yet.

qa.q: If you were Dilnaz, what would you want for Payal here?
qa.a: You would want her to keep trying but not end up in tears, so offering to try together gives help without taking over.

grounding: A toddler stretches on tiptoe toward a toy, trying one hand and then the other, while her mother comments and offers help.

subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
passage: Rain tapped the window of the flat in Lyon while Clara, not yet two, eyed her knitted elephant on the bookshelf. She jumped; it stayed put. She grabbed the shelf edge and tugged; the shelf didn't budge. Then she noticed the little lace mat under the elephant, its corner hanging down, and yanked it. The elephant slid a finger's width. Clara gasped, yanked again, and again, watching it creep closer. Her childminder Wanjiru stayed near, smiling.

qa.q: What hung down from under the elephant?
qa.a: The corner of the little lace mat under the elephant hung down.

qa.q: What did Clara feel when the elephant finally moved?
qa.a: She gasped and yanked again at once, which shows she was thrilled that this move finally worked.

qa.q: What else could Clara try if the mat stopped working?
qa.a: She could turn to Wanjiru and point, since asking a grown-up is another way to reach what she cannot.

qa.q: What might Wanjiru be thinking while watching the mat trick?
qa.a: Wanjiru is probably amused and impressed, staying near and smiling in case the elephant tumbles down.

grounding: A toddler tries jumping, tugging the shelf and pulling a mat, then keeps repeating the one move that makes the toy shift.

subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
passage: I'm Anjali from the flat next door, and on Sunday I was minding Irfan. His rubber elephant sat on a folded mat on the low window ledge, the fringe dangling. First he jumped, feet barely leaving the floor. Then he tugged at the ledge itself. Then he caught the fringe and pulled, and the elephant shivered toward him. He pulled again, and again, humming. Was he planning? I couldn't tell. I just knelt close in case it dropped on his head.

qa.q: Where was Irfan's rubber elephant?
qa.a: It sat on a folded mat on the low window ledge.

qa.q: What was Anjali feeling while watching Irfan?
qa.a: Anjali was curious and a little unsure, wondering whether Irfan was really planning, and cautious enough to kneel close.

qa.q: Which approach might help Irfan reach the elephant faster?
qa.a: Pointing and asking Anjali for help would work at once, though his pulling test teaches him which move actually shifts the toy.

qa.q: What might the game be like for Irfan?
qa.a: It is probably exciting for him: each pull makes the elephant shiver closer, so he hums and keeps doing it.

grounding: An observer watches a toddler try jumping, tugging and pulling a mat, and repeat whichever move shifts the toy.

subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf

Hansa banged it at once, beaming.

subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
passage: On Sunday in the Chennai flat, Yamini watched her cousin Sharmila drag the small plastic stool to the bookshelf, step up and pull down a picture book. Later, alone, Yamini shoved that very stool over toward the shelf where her doll sat. It bumped onto the edge of the doormat and tilted. Yamini climbed anyway, one knee then the other, just as Sharmila had. The stool rocked. Sharmila ran over and held it steady.

qa.q: What did Sharmila pull down from the bookshelf?
qa.a: She pulled down a picture book.

qa.q: What was Yamini thinking as she pushed the stool over?
qa.a: She seemed eager and confident, sure that doing exactly what Sharmila did would bring the doll down too.

qa.q: What would you change first to make Yamini's copying safer?
qa.a: Place the stool on flat floor and have a grown-up or Sharmila hold it, because the plan was good but the spot was not steady.

qa.q: How might Sharmila feel seeing Yamini copy her?
qa.a: Sharmila is probably alarmed at the rocking stool, and maybe a little flattered that Yamini copied her.

grounding: A toddler copies her cousin's stool-climbing to reach a shelf without checking whether the stool stands steady.

"Watch, Thomas. Stool, step, up!" Rukmini chechi dragged the stool over and climbed. "See? Got my comb."

He grabbed it and shoved it across the floor, straight onto a rumpled bedsheet.
"Thomas, wait, that's all bunched up!"

passage: The clay bullock sat in the wall niche of the mud house, and Madhuri wanted it. She stood beneath it, arm high, stretching and stretching from one place while hens scratched outside. The wooden patla stood by the doorway, three steps away. She never looked at it. Minutes passed. Her lip wobbled, then tears came. Pankaj Mama, back from the field, lifted her and said softly, "Next time, call me."

qa.a: The wooden patla stood by the doorway, three steps away.

qa.a: She was frustrated and sad after stretching for so long with nothing to show for it.

subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
passage: At the Cape Town daycare, Zanele stood under the cubby shelf, straining toward a yellow bus. She reached, dropped, reached again, always from the same square of carpet. "Let's look around together, Zanele. What could help?"

qa.a: Pausing to look around, spotting the step stool or asking Olga, because repeating one failing reach only adds tears.

qa.q: How does Olga see Zanele's struggle?
qa.a: Olga sees that Zanele is stuck on one move, so she stays calm and invites her to look for other ideas rather than just grabbing the bus.

Maria aunty, the nanny, watched from the doorway, waiting to see what came next.

qa.a: The box held murukku.

qa.a: She is probably curious and impatient, dropping each move quickly when it doesn't open the box.

qa.a: Maria aunty seems interested and patient, letting her explore before stepping in.

At drop-off today Nilesh watched his papa, Anand, unscrew the steel tiffin to show me his lunch. At snack time he picked up the small box of raisins and turned his wrist exactly the way Papa had. subtopic: Opening a plastic container
